utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances for today, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, assisted by Crispian Smith for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic and Miroslav Cuskic for Zupljanin Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Would the Usher kindly escort the witness back to the stand, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Tutus. Before I invite Ms. Korner to resume her examination-in-chief, I would remind you you're still on your oath. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... just as well, I haven't got the mic on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, I am afraid I just want to go back over a couple of things we dealt with towards the end of yesterday. You told the Court yesterday, when we were dealing with the SOS, that you had prosecuted members of the SOS. Do you actually mean prosecution, or do you mean filing a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, did I what the organs of internal affairs have to do. That's what I had in mind, and what they had to do was to file criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Could you tell us against which members of the SOS you filed criminal reports?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember any individual cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just want to check with you. Are you sure that you actually filed criminal reports in respect of members of the SOS, as members of the SOS, as opposed to filing criminal reports against members of the SOS who went into the Special Police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was thinking of members of those groups, those men from the SOS, who, at the time, committed various crimes. They took gold, stole gold, jewelry, they did that sort of thing. So there was theft at the check-points, and whenever there were document, evidence, the citizens would report those cases and would -- then we would process the crimes. That's what I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And you can't now remember any names?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't. The crime police was involved in that. I know this was done, but I can't remember any individual names.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. The other matter I want to go back over is this. That we looked yesterday at the newspaper article, where Mr. Zupljanin was -- was talking about the formation of the Special Police. And, in particular, said that members of the SOS would be incorporated. And you said that, in your view -- I better just find your exact words. Yes, it was just before you were talking about prosecuting them. And ... you said that you -- you -- you didn't know about that until you may have read the article. Do you remember? You said: "I did not know that the SOS was placed under the jurisdiction of the CSB." And that's at page 66 of the unrevised LiveNote. I want to go back to the -- the meetings that were being held at the time of the SOS appearance on the barricades which you spoke about. And you said that you had been there when Predrag Radic was there, and there were discussions being held about what was to be done about the SOS. Do you remember telling us about that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. Now, this is a matter you were asked about in your interview, and, if necessary, you can refresh your memory from it. Was there any discussion with Mr. Radic about whether the SOS should go into the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But not into the reserve police. There was discussion about the fact that the SOS members should be used to form a Special Police unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So that was -- there was discussion on the day that they were there, with the barricades up, on the 3rd of April, as to whether they should form a Special Police unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was towards the end of the negotiations. It wasn't on the first day. Perhaps on the third or fourth. Towards the end, when all the events had come to an end.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But you say this was -- this wasn't on the first day. The whole incident with the barricades and the negotiations only lasted one day.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the discussions about how to solve their status continued for the following two or three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And who was involved in those discussions?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, President Radic convened a brief meeting. We were there with him, and he asked that I use that group of men to form a Special Police unit, as part of the Banja Luka SJB, and I refused to do this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll come on to your refusal in a moment. When you say "we," who else was there, apart from you and President Radic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I remember that Milan Puvacic, Jovo Rosic were there. At one of the last meetings, General Kelecevic was present, the Chief of Staff of the 1st Krajina Corps, and he supported me at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, but, well, what about Mr. Zupljanin as -- as the chief of the CSB? Was he present at any of these discussions?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Radoslav Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether he was there from the beginning, but I do believe that he did appear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, you say that you refused. And what was the reason for your refusal?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the reason was that I was convinced that police forces can only be formed in accordance with the law, and that is the responsibility of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So you're saying, are you, that you didn't have the authority to form a Special Police unit within the SJB?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have such authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. So you refused. Did your refusal have anything to do with the fact that by then you knew that at least some of the people in the SOS were convicted criminals?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regardless of that fact, I wouldn't have accepted establishing such units, even if they hadn't been criminals, because that was against the law. But, yes, that was an additional factor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So let's go back to when the -- when Mr. Zupljanin announced in a press conference about the formation of this Special Police unit into which members of the SOS would be absorbed. In the light of what you had already said to Mr. Radic and others when the suggestion was made, did you raise the question with Mr. Zupljanin as to what authority he had to do this and whether the SOS were the right people to put into a Special Police unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that, at the end of the second or third day, after those events, we were sitting next to each other in President Radic's office, myself and Mr. Zupljanin. And on that occasion, they asked me -- Radic kept saying, Vlado, have you decided to accept these people? And I kept saying that I stood by my initial position, and it was out of the question for these men to become part of a unit within the SJB. Then they tried to persuade Mr. Radic [as interpreted] that the town wasn't sufficiently secure and that was the reason for which they were insisting that about 200 young men should be accepted into a unit; it would increase the safety in town. I said that as for safety in the town it was for me to assess whether it was safe or not. He asked me what the safety situation was like and I said that it was fairly satisfactory. He insisted on increasing the level of safety in town. I then suggested that if the social and political community and he, as the president, want the safety to be increased, then the -- it was necessary to reserve -- to mobilise the reserve TO in accordance with the law. They would then protect the bridges, the streets, and so on. I said that this is how we would increase security. He again insisted on having this unit and then asked me to get into the car with him and to drive around town. Then I asked, Stojan, I said, Stole, what do you want me to do? And he said calmly, quietly, Well, Vlado, what are you going to do now? Go and look around. I saw that he wasn't very willing and I saw that he understood why I was refusing to act in a certain way. But pressure was being exerted on him for him to do that. I then went off with President Radic. I said, Well, if they continue on insisting on this, I won't appear anymore. Then Stole said, Vlado, leave it, go around town. So I did. On the following day there was another meeting and then General Kelecevic appeared and President Radic asked me again whether I had changed my opinion and whether I would accept those men as a unit. I said, Very well, into the reserve force but as individuals, and they must previously be checked. He then reacted and said, Well, it is not necessary to check them. I said that men who had a criminal record couldn't become part of the reserve police force. Kelecevic then got up and said to President Radic, he said, President, Mr. Tutus is [Realtime transcript read in error "isn't"] right, don't ask him to do that. He said, General, is that something you mean? And the General said, Yes, I'm serious about that. And that was the end. No one then called me after that or put any questions to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Ms. Korner. There a couple of things which have not been recorded correctly. First of all, page 6, line 13: "Then they tried to persuade," I believe the witness said "me" not "Mr. Radic." It was Mr. Radic who was trying to persuade him. That's line 13. And page 7, 10: "He said, President, Mr. Tutus is right," not isn't. It is recorded "isn't right." But the witness said -- he was quoting what the General said and General said, "President, Mr. Tutus is right." Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I accept that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to just pursue this matter of the suggestion that there was insufficient officers to maintain security in the town. By this time, April 1992, had there been a mobilisation of the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I think so. I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, again, you were asked about this in your interview at page 75. And was the figure when -- or the numbers of police which had been mobilised, I would suggest, way back in 1991, something in the reason to 5 to 600?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's between 4 and 500, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You said 4 -- but you think 4 to 500 rather than 5 to 600?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, in addition to the regular police employees which you had about -- you told us around 250 to 260, there were the further 4 to 500 reserve police officers?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the -- the system. But I don't think they were all mobilised. I think that the mobilisation was only up to 50 per cent, not 100 per cent of the forces had been mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. But in any event, you had considerably more men at your disposal than there were members of the SOS. Is that a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, we had more men. I was told there were about 200 of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, thank you. That's all I want to ask about those matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Can I just put a question to Mr. Tutus, and I apologise if I have misunderstood the -- the -- the circumstances or -- that were present in this discussion about whether or not the members of the SOS could or should become members of a new Special Police unit. Because you told us that Radic put this proposal to you. And my question is: Can you tell us in which capacity Mr. Radic wanted to establish this new police unit? I'm especially, of course, asking, again, into the question of whether or not Mr. Radic was acting in his capacity as member of the Crisis Staff or his membership of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] His position in the discussion was that of a -- the president of the Assembly. He was at the head of the negotiation team that spoke to SOS representatives. And that's where the idea was born. The idea that some of them - that's how I understood it - should be included in the police forces as a unit. And as a member of the negotiation team, as the head of the negotiation team this is what he requested. But, naturally, he played the role of president and I believe that he wanted to solve that problem. Someone promised them that that would be done, and he tried to reach a peaceful solution through negotiations. And I think one of the conditions was that, that they should become a police unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. But was the Municipal Assembly still alive and in force at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, everything functioned, except that day when that happened wasn't normal, but the institutions remained. They operated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we now move -- could we now move, please, on in the month of May of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And could you have a look, please, at a document which is P561. This is from the CSB, addressed to all -- it's a dispatch addressed to the chief of all public security stations. And if we look at the bottom in the B/C/S, you can see it comes from Mr. Zupljanin. Yeah. This document is about the seizure of illegally owned weapons, et cetera, and all I want to ask but is this. It starts: "In keeping with the decision of the Autonomous Region of the Bosnian Krajina regarding the surrender of illegally owned weapons and ammunition ..." and refers to the previous dispatches, "public security stations must undertake the following ..." Now, this follows on from Mr. Zupljanin saying publicly that the Special Police are going to be formed as a result of the decision by the Assembly of the autonomous region. Here is he referring to the decision for the surrender of weapons. Now, as chief did you get a copy of this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you notice that -- that, again, the decision of the Autonomous Region of Krajina was being referred to?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you quite frankly, I didn't pay attention at the time. Now I can see it, but whether I gave it any thought at the time, I really couldn't say. Maybe it caught my eye; I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And just dealing with that, did you in fact put into place concrete plans for the seizure of illegal weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did undertake activities following this dispatch, and we worked actively to seize weapons. We even toured local communes. President Radic and I, together, told all the local communes in Banja Luka and appealed to citizens, if they owned illegal weapons without being a part of the police force or the VRS to surrender them and they would not be subject to prosecution if they did so. We toured a lot of communes and the representatives of the Catholic church attended some of the meetings. I can't remember if there were any representatives of the Islamic community, but I know that somebody from the Catholic church was with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would that have been Bishop Komarica?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about Bishop Komarica. I believe one of the lower-ranking priests went.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did illegal weapons include those who had permits for hunting rifles?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Illegal weapons mean weapons owned without a licence. Or perhaps a weapon that was issued by the army by somebody who later deserted without returning the weapon, and it was our aim to seize such weapons. The police force was tasked to also seize weapons from those who had licences but were of interest to the security forces, were estimated to be a threat, or who had deserted. We intended to later return these weapons to these people. But we -- our main objective was to enhance security in town.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And who was -- when you say -- sorry. When you say "a threat," do you mean a threat to the security of the Serb Republic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I used the word "threat." I said we wanted to raise security culture to a higher level.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, the translation and what you were recorded as saying, literally a few seconds ago, was: "... the police force was tasked to also seize weapons from those who ... were estimated to be a threat, or who had deserted." That's why I'm asking you why -- a threat to whom, or what?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word "threat" was a misinterpretation. The exact word I used was individuals of security interest. That is, people who are estimated by the police on the ground to have violated military regulations by deserting and from such people we seized weapons. Known criminals also, alcoholics, people bent on violations of law and public order. It was up to the police officers on the ground to make an appraisal, an evaluation, and decide from whom they would seize weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Was the seizure of legally owned hunting rifles from people who -- from individuals of security interest, did that target any one nationality in particular, or more than one?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the Law on the Possession of Weapons and Ammunition, there was an article that authorised us to seize even legal weapons when it is estimated that the possession of such a weapon may be a jeopardy to the security of the country or public order. I think that's the phrasing. You could not target an ethnic group. It's a matter of estimate aimed at any citizen who is evaluated in this way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, we're now back to where we were originally, which is a threat to security effectively. Here you call it "a jeopardy to the security of the country." Which nationalities were considered to be a threat to the security of the Serbian state?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bosnia and Herzegovina, a civil war was going on. On one side were Serbs and on the other side were Croats and Muslims. And between these ethnic groups, war was being waged.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I think we're getting there. Is it -- is it your evidence that, in fact, because of what you say was a civil war, it was the Croats and the Muslims in the Banja Luka area who were being targeted for the removal of lawfully owned hunting rifles?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You couldn't say that they were targeted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's move on. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we move now, please, to the document, which is -- sorry. Yes, it's document, please, number P1013, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is a communication from the Ministry of Interior which is being forwarded by Mr. Zupljanin to the chiefs. And it deals with the -- what is called unprincipled behaviour among the police reserve force in certain public security stations, and a collegium of ministers decided that persons convicted of criminal acts, except those related to traffic, et cetera, cannot be part of the police reserves. And employees who do not fulfil the conditions prescribed for the police reserves are to return their equipment to the police stations to be placed at the disposal of the Serbian Territorial Defence. Now did that affect any of the reserve police attached to your SJB?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand we received this dispatch. The reserve police force under my command was from before the war. We had a full complement already before the war and it was implied, that was the regulation that people with a criminal record could not be admitted into the reserve force. The reserve force was clean. However, if there had been some oversights later in individual cases and somebody was admitted without meeting the standards, we -- we followed this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So at the time of the 18th of May, are you saying that nobody in the reserve police force at -- under your authority fell into the category of those who had been convicted of a criminal act?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that there were no cases at all, but there were certainly very few. But we certainly honoured this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, very briefly, can we look, please, at document number P1017.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The month is illegible but it seems to say, on the B/C/S, according to the translation, but it -- it refers to previous dispatches on the 11th and the 14th of May, and I think, actually, it's probably the 1st of June, if it's the 1st of anything, because it says: "All SJBs are obliged to submit to the centre detailed information on the disarmament operations up to and to inclusive of the 15th of June." And did you get this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you submit the detailed information that was requested?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm convinced we replied.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now I want you to look -- thank you very much. That's all I ask about that document. Can you look very briefly, please, because it's not a document that you may have seen before you saw it at this court, at document number 1159. This is a handwritten document which comes from Bosanska Kostajnica branch police station. Now, where is Bosanska Kostajnica?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: West of Prijedor, from Novi Grad on to Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the Una river.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right and it came within the area of responsibility of the CSB Banja Luka, did it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I object to this document and this line of questioning. Bosanska Kostajnica is not part of the indictment against the accused here. I do not see the relevance of showing this document or any questions on this municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If Mr. Krgovic waits a moment -- I absolutely accept it is not in the indictment and the reason I'm asking about is not to ask about this, but as you will see, whether the same sort of complaint was delivered to Mr. Tutus. This is a complaint about the search of Muslim houses in the area of Bosanska Kostajnica, and the complaint is the behaviour of the people who did the search, seizure of weapons for which citizens possess valid licence, et cetera, et cetera. And the station commander who wrote this said: "This kind of behaviour damages the reputation of police officers because it was also citizens of Serbian nationality who drew our attention to these omissions." What I want to ask you is whether you received, Mr. Tutus, or your commanders, complaints that were similar to this one about the behaviour of the police officers who were conducting these searches?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why then do we need this document? Isn't it simpler to put the question? Why refer to this document which has nothing to do with it. The witness has not seen it before and it had nothing to do with his job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner, why not just ask the question about behaviour of -- of this nature? Because introducing this document, which you certainly aren't going to exhibit through this witness, isn't going to advance the matter, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not going to seek to exhibit it through the witness. I said I didn't think he saw it before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So, as Mr. Krgovic said, why not just simply go directly to the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I could go directly to the question, and I am now going to ask the question, and I have asked the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tutus, sorry about that intervention. Could you tell us, did you have similar complaints to this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of Banja Luka, as the document says in the first sentence, a thorough search began of Muslim houses. We in Banja Luka did not have such an organised search of houses. This was a regular activity by regular police forces, and we did not get many complaints against the organised seizure of weapons, but we had incidents with individual members of the Special Police detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What, who were carrying out these types of searches?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the area of Banja Luka, they did not conduct any searches in joint action with the police. This job was done by the regular police. And if anyone committed a violation, entered an apartment illegally or did something else illegally, the person was subject to prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. What I was asking was whether, as a result of the searches that your police officers were carrying out, did you receive any complaints about arrogant behaviour by your police officers?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not get any complaints about arrogant behaviour by our police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you get complaints from anybody that you were seizing weapons for which the owners had a permit?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not get any complaints.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did your -- any of the officers under your command, such as the commander of your police station, get any complaints?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. At least I did not hear any complaints at the meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. You're sure about this, are you, you never had any complaints?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be sure. There may have been complaints that I don't remember, or maybe somebody else got complaints that they did not share with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Because you looked at this document, didn't you, on Sunday?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we move then, please, to the document which is P173. Actually, no, don't worry. I'm sorry. We can forget that because it's addressed to the chief and it's already an exhibit. I'm just going to check this one. Yes, actually, Your Honour, we can move on. Sorry. It was a document he was asked about in interview but I don't know that it takes us much further. Yes, number -- document, please, 131 -- sorry, P565.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, this is a document from -- from your SJB, and, in fact, it's a response to a request from Mr. Zupljanin. It's addressed to the CSB or from the CSB. "We hereby inform that you Banja Luka SJB has no information regarding paramilitary organisations [sic] in the ... Banja Luka municipality." And it's signed: "Section chief, Mr. Zoran Josic." Was Mr. Josic, I think when we looked at your diagram, was he the chief of your crime section?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And would he have consulted with you before he sent a response?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he would.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And do you consider that this was accurate in -- on the 18th of May?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you'd had no incursions into the Banja Luka area of any paramilitary groups?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, that's the next question. What did you consider the SOS to be, then?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SOS was already neutralised by the time this was written. And I saw here a piece of information shown to me by the Prosecution, where the SOS is qualified as a paramilitary formation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the next document I'm going to show you. So -- but from your point of view, and Mr. Josic's, you didn't consider that the SOS was worth mentioning because, in your view, it was neutralised. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I ask that be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, it's already an exhibit, is it? Oh, yes, it is. I said it was. All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Let's have a look, please, at the document that you've just referred to, which I think is - just a moment - which you had a chance to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, could we have P591. I think we need to go to the last page in each. It's the sixth page in English. I think it's the same in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's -- the report was actually authored by Colonel Tolimir who was then the intelligence officer for the VRS who would -- then became General Tolimir. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who's on trial in another court at this moment; is that right? Or don't you know?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether he is on trial. But now I know that he is in The Hague Tribunal's detention unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And as you -- it's a report headed -- if we go back to the first page. Dated much later, in fact, 28th of July. On the paramilitary formations in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it talks about a number of these paramilitary groups. Some of which -- the names are familiar, Arkan's Men, Seselj's men, Captain Dragan, the Wolves of Vucak. Main characteristics very often such units have in their ranks, pathological criminals. And then if we go down the page a little bit. Frequent links between paramilitaries and corrupt political leaderships. And then if we look, please, at the third page in English and the third page in B/C/S. Do you see -- I think it's the last paragraph in -- on the left hand -- in the -- in B/C/S. And it's the - one, two, three, four, five - sixth paragraph. The Serbian Radical Party of SRBH established a War Staff in Banja Luka headed by a commander Nikodin Cavic, a Banja Luka lawyer. A great part of formation consists of volunteers from Serbia, and so on and so forth. Were you aware of this activity - and I agree this is now July - of the -- the War Staff of the Serbian Radical Party and Mr. Cavic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't familiar with those activities, but did I know Nikodin Cavic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you know that he was a member of the Serb Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were rumours according to which he was a member of the Serb Radical Party. But I personally didn't see a document showing that he had joined.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You told us a few minutes ago about the information you had about people who were a threat, using -- paraphrasing what you actually said, to the Serbian -- to the state. Was this man considered, as a result of information you had, to be such a threat?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Ms. Korner, because there is some mistake in transcript. It is page 21, line 30, witness said -- line 14, sorry. He said: "I wasn't familiar with those activities but I" -- but witness says, "but I didn't see" --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: "I didn't see the card that he was a member of the -- Mr. Cavic."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think that's right [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll say it in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just ask you, Mr. Tutus, again, so we clear this up. Did you know Mr. Cavic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you know that he was a member of the Serb Radical Party?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were rumours, according to which he was a member, but I didn't know that, in the sense that I didn't see his membership card. It wasn't apparent that he was involved in political activities. He was someone to whom you wouldn't perhaps pay much attention ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So, although, apparently Colonel Tolimir got intelligence about this man, you didn't get any intelligence to suggest that he was a member of the Serb Radical Party establishing a War Staff?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And so are you able to tell us whether you removed any weapons from him?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that's out of the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then can we go, please, to the fourth page in English and the fifth page, I think it is, in B/C/S. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You will see, as you said yourself, because you saw the document on Sunday, that, on the -- oh, no, sorry, we're in the ... the wrong page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Fourth page in English, please. That's right. Sorry, just right. Yes, just the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you see the SOS is referred to there? "Under the command of Nenad Stevandic, also president of the Serbian Sokol Society ... private businessmen ... some senior SJB and SNB officials in Banja Luka CSB have considerable influence over the SOS, but many infamous Banja Luka criminals have joined the SOS. Part of the SOS formations ... was officially disbanded joined the Banja Luka CSB Special Police detachment but is not really under the control of the detachments command or the CSB," and so on. In July, Colonel Tolimir's information was that this group was classed as a paramilitary group; but you, in May, didn't think it worthy of mentioning?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason not to believe Colonel Tolimir. This is military terminology. He knows what paramilitary units and so on and so forth are. Perhaps we didn't recognise them as a paramilitary unit. But if that's what he said, well, there's no reason for me to doubt that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you think who might be meant by the "senior SJB officials who might have considerable -- who have considerable influence over the SOS"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said "senior." I don't see the term "senior officials" here. I just see the terms "some officials."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, which is the word -- wait a minute, just let me get the ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, let's find this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Which is the word you say is "some" and not "senior"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the third one. The third word in this second paragraph on this page. The Serbian Defence Forces from Banja Luka under the command of Stevandic and so on and so forth. That's where it is. It's a little lower down. That's the one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you read out, please, so that I can -- we can get a translation through the earphones. Could you read out the word -- from the word -- just a moment. The sentence which begins: "Private businessmen ..."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Significant influence on the SOS is exercised by private businessmen and some officials from the SJB and SNB in the Banja Luka CSB."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So the word "senior" does not appear there anywhere. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I can't see that word.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So it just says "some SJB"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Some." That's right. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, is that --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I saw Mr. Cvijetic nodding. But is -- I would like confirmation before I ask for a new translation that the word "senior" doesn't appear. It does appear.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes that the word "senior" does not appear. Only the word "some."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I apologise for that. You're absolutely right to correct that, but it doesn't actually affect the question except for the "senior." Any idea who the "some SJB and SNB" -- let's leave SNB out of it. "Some SJB ... officials ... who have an influence -- considerable influence over the SOS," might be?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, that's all I want to ask about this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'd like to have a look, please, at the document which is P367. So we're going back in time to May.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's dated in handwriting the 21st of May, but the actual date of the dispatch is the 20th of May. And it's a record of the conclusions reached at the expanded meeting of the centre council held on the 6th of May. And it's addressed to the chief -- addressed to all SJBs in the region except Jajce. And again if we look at the last page in the English and the last page in the B/C/S, we'll see that it bears the name of Stojan Zupljanin. Now you told us yesterday, you weren't a member of the collegium, but were you -- would you have attended -- and, indeed, we can see if we look at the attendees -- sorry, paragraph 1, back to the first page. In the fifth line of the first paragraph, the meeting was attended by the chiefs of the public security stations in Banja Luka, et cetera, et cetera. So you were at this meeting, is that right, because it was an expanded meeting, if you like?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I wasn't at the collegium, but I was in attendance at the professional council.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, before we look at the parts that I want to ask you about, in fact, for the English, and I think you corrected this when you were asked about this in interview. If you go to Agenda 1 --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go to the bottom and then can we pull up the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- it talks about the speakers who spoke after Mr. Zupljanin. Then we get Stevan Markovic and then Milorad -- it's put in the English as Djuricic but I think you corrected that. It's Mr. Djuric, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And we can see all the various people who spoke. Now can we go, please, to the summing up done by Chief Stojan Zupljanin, which is on the second page in the English, and the proposal of the conclusions, and it's the second page in B/C/S as well. Paragraph 2: "Starting today until further notice, all chiefs of public security stations must wear a uniform. The uniform must be either a new blue camouflage uniform or the usual police uniform." It says "starting today." Was it not usual for the chiefs of police to wear a uniform? The chief of public security stations, rather.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some wore uniforms; others didn't. There were no strict rules.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And do you know why Mr. Zupljanin was saying, from now on, everybody had to wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably because some of them weren't wearing uniforms, and he wanted them all to be in uniform. That's the only way I could interpret this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then item 4: "All my orders conveyed orally, as well as those I may forward by dispatch, must be carried out: They are your law." Well, first of all, as far as the law was concerned, was that right, that Mr. Zupljanin's orders, conveyed orally or in writing, had to be carried out?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had to be carried out. The ones that were in accordance with the law. And in my understanding, his orders wouldn't contravene the law. Those orders had to be carried out. Orders that were not in accordance were -- with the law didn't have to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's a fairly forceful statement. You knew Mr. Zupljanin pretty well. Was that his normal way of speaking?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all I can conclude, on the basis of -- I can only draw conclusions and I can only say what my own opinion is on the basis of this item. Doesn't mean I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no. I'm asking you, from your knowledge of Mr. Zupljanin, who you have known for -- since effectively police school, over 15 years by then, was that his normal way of delivering instructions?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that they're his words, addressed to those who acted in an arrogant way in the field. He wanted them to act in a more serious way. I think that was the objective, because there were quieter people from the SJB who weren't familiar with the rules. They had been normal citizens before. There could have been problems. So I assume that this was also the reason for which such strict language was used.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: During remember being asked the very self-same question when you were interviewed by Mr. Sebire?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember what I answered on that occasion. That was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would it help you to refresh your memory if you had a look at what you said then?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you think it is essential, that's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll ask the question again and then, if necessary, we'll remind you. From your working with Mr. Zupljanin for many years now, can you tell us if he was in the habit of delivering orders in a forceful manner?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, he's not a person who uses tough language. He might address, use serious language but in a calm manner. And I wouldn't say that he said exactly what is stated here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, let's see if we can refresh your memory from what you said to Mr. Sebire in interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: To what end, Ms. Korner? I would have thought that the last question you put to him is what the relevant question is for these purposes. His assessment, his appreciation, his recollection of the way that Mr. Zupljanin gave orders or gave instructions. What he would have said on a previous occasion, I'm not sure how it assists.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think it does assist because it was said during the course of this interview it's a very clear statement and it is not exactly what he said here. I'm simply asking him to refresh his memory and see if he still agrees with that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I'm not sure why you're setting up a contradiction of your own witness. But go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have up, please, on the screen --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You, in fact, I think, have a got a copy of your own in your own language but you probably haven't got it with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we have page 136 of 65 ter 9026. No, page 136, please. I have no idea where it is in the B/C/S version, I'm afraid, because I didn't appreciate that we had a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But in English, the -- Mr. Sebire said to you, on this very point: "It's quite a strong statement that he made, in the sense that whatever he orders or says has to be the law." And your response was: "Well, he had a habit of speaking in that way." Now, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: So, this was leading question and the answer was like that. In direct examination the witness said what he said. What's the point of that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm asking him, Mr. Krgovic, whether, having refreshed his memory of what he said to Mr. Sebire in 2004, he sticks to this statement that Mr. Zupljanin had a habit of speaking in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: It's cross-examination. It's not examination-in-chief. That's my point.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm just asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That's exactly the flag that I raised earlier. But please proceed, Ms. Korner. I expect I understand why she is taking this route.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Tutus, we've spent a long time on this, and I'd like to move on. First of all -- not, first of all, do you agree that that's what you told Mr. Sebire in 2004?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's roughly what I said in the courtroom just a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Anyhow, so that's right, is it? This is how he spoke or he had a habit of speaking in this way. Yes or no, Mr. Tutus?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have answered that question. There's nothing in particular I would like to add.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's go back, then, please, to the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, it's 10.20. It is past the time that we usually take a break, if --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we go back to the document that we were looking at before, please, which is -- whatever it was. It was document P367. Can we go to the second page, please, in B/C/S, and the second page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Paragraph 5 says -- after the one we were talking about, "my orders." "We have to identify in time those among us who are involved in criminal activities and we must take rigorous steps against them (immediately commence disciplinary proceedings)." When Mr. Zupljanin was saying "those among us," did you understand him to be talking about police officers?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand it as referring to all employees of the Security Services Centre, in the broader sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Paragraph 12 of the proposed conclusions, which you will find on the third page in English, and it's the bottom of that page in B/C/S. It says: "Chiefs of departments in the CSB headquarters and chiefs of public security stations will submit monthly performance reports and plans for the current month to me by the fifth of each month. I will deduct 10 per cent of the chief's income for every failure to submit a report on time." First, had that happened before, the threat of deduction of income, if reports weren't delivered on time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Are you aware of anybody who had 10 per cent of their income deducted for failure?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was never done to me. I don't know about others.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we then go to number 23 of the conclusions, which is on the fourth page in English, and it's the fourth page in B/C/S as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: "In all our activities, we are obliged to observe all measures and apply all procedures ordered by the Crisis Staff of the autonomous region." So, Mr. Tutus, Mr. Zupljanin made it clear to all of you at the meeting that -- that the Crisis Staff of the region had authority; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In point 23, it says exactly as you read.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then it talks about the disarmament dead-line and saying that no action should be taken until the Crisis Staff makes the relevant decisions. And, finally, just to note at the end of this document, Agenda item 3, which we will see on the fifth page in English and the same in B/C/S. This is the reference to Mr. Zupljanin establishing a special counter-sabotage and counter-terrorist police unit of about 150, and it's to be made up of active reserve policemen and persons who fought on the Western Slavonia battle-fronts. And that's a reference obviously to the parade we watched at the end of yesterday. All right. Thank you. Can we -- I'm sorry, we have to go back in time a little. I'm sorry, I missed out two documents by mistake yesterday, three ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we look, please, at document -- it is already an exhibit, P355.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because it's the meeting a month before, roughly, because that meeting we looked at was 6th of May. This meeting took place -- not roughly, exactly on the 6th of April. Conclusions, when we enlarge, centre -- it's called "Centre Council Session," held on the 6th of April, and it's sent to you and all the chiefs of the SJBs. So were you -- do we take it you were present at this meeting as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, was it -- was it the habit that once a month there would be a meeting of the expanded, as it were, collegium, or the centre council?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were meetings. We met often. I can't say now exactly whether it was twice a month or once a month. But we met as required, as the chief of the centre convened.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I just want to ask you about one matter concerned in this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look at the second page in English and the second page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Zupljanin saying that -- he established the following conclusion: "The Banja Luka CSB shall be organised in accordance with the constitution and shall consist of all public security stations whose municipal assemblies declare themselves in favour of joining the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Thus, in addition to the existing ones, the centre shall also be joined by the following public security stations ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if we go, please, in English to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We see amongst those that were coming under the CSB, included what's described as the Serb Municipality of Prijedor, and the Serb Municipality of Sanski Most. Now, you came from Sanski Most. Were you still living there at the time, at this period, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I lived in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Were you aware before this meeting that there were -- there was a Serb Municipality of Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serb Municipality Sanski Most was established in Ostra Luka after the armed conflict in Sanski Most. That's what I know. But I cannot tell you the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But this is the 11th of -- well, I'm sorry, the meeting was the 6th of April, 1992. By the 6th of April, 1992, there had been no armed conflict, had there, in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I cannot be sure about the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. At this -- all I'm asking is, at this meeting on the 6th of April, before this was announced, had you been aware that, in particular, there was now something called the Serb Municipality of Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That existed; I'm aware of that. And the seat, the base was in Ostra Luka. And to this day, there is a Serb Municipality Sanski Most there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There is, is there? All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's leave that, please, and then just look briefly at document P354, which was MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Which is the same day as the other document was sent out. Again, it's addressed to, apart from the republic MUP, the chiefs of the SJBs. And it's obviously referring to criticism of the formation of the Serbian MUP. But then it says this in the second paragraph: "All employees found that work in the organs of the Serb Republic ... are given an opportunity to express their decision regarding the maintenance of employment ... with no pressure by the 15th of April." And: "They are to sign a formal statement in accordance with the Law on Internal Affairs of the Serb Republic ... this should be no different from the statement of the ex-minister of internal affairs and should have nothing to do with the so-called statement of loyalty, as it was noted in the dispatch ..." Do you remember receiving this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably received it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And we discussed yesterday the question of the statement of loyalty or whatever it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, all I'm asking now is that it can be formally exhibited. It was MFI'd before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry -- Your Honours, I'm so sorry. On my spreadsheet, it appeared as MFI'd, but I'm told that it was already put in. All right. I'm sorry we wasted time on that. Can we now move back to the period of time we were looking at. Well, we could if I was able to find my list. Yes. Your Honours, I'm so sorry for this delay but I'm aware that I'm running shortly out of time, and I'm trying to cut out documents which are already exhibits. So that's why I ... Yes. Could we look, please ... no, don't need that one either. Yes. Document ... 2505.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, this is one of many documents, I think, Mr. Tutus, that you actually gave to the investigator during the course of your interview. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it was a whole series of documents which we will look at, I hope fairly quickly, concerning reports made by you about the behaviour of the Special Police; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This one dated the 4th of June of 1992 concerning a -- an altercation between the Banja Luka Budzak police station -- police officers and members of the Special Police at some catering facilities in Banja Luka; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if we look, please, at the second page in English, and it's still on the first page in B/C/S. It's -- under 2 in B/C/S, the second paragraph: "The behaviour of the special detachment members is contrary to the prescribed norms and regulations for employees of internal affairs organs, which is visible in their arrogant and violent behaviour, their evasion of legal provisions of the Banja Luka" -- I think that should be SJB, "police officers, and even in the commission of criminal acts which are being officially prosecuted." Then you go on to say -- in the next page you list a number of incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next page in English, same page in B/C/S, I think. The next page -- sorry, the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The dispatches which you had already reported in May. Problems at the Centar police station, Goran Popovic, and an apartment being broken into. And then a pistol being taken from somebody's apartment in Banja Luka. And you signed this report, didn't you.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So there had been an earlier report, on the 22nd of May, about the behaviour of one of the special brigades; is that right -- or Special Police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now let's go --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be marked, please -- admitted and marked, and we will go through the rest of them fairly quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P1081, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we go now, please, to 2506, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I didn't catch from the document to whom these reports are sent. I assume it's to the CSB but I didn't see it. Can you confirm?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I think that these were sent --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, perhaps you can confirm: This was being sent to the CSB, is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see the first page to see whom it was addressed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, it was, I can assure you, but let's go back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, we'll have to have the -- not this document, the one before that. Whatever the number was, please, can we have that back. 2505. Very quickly, front page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There we can see -- needn't bother with anything else. CSB Banja Luka, right? Report of the 4th of June?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was submitted to the Ministry of the Interior and their Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. Sorry, you're absolute right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And thank you, Your Honour. Just goes to show how you shouldn't go through them too quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's also addressed to the Minister of the Interior -- the Ministry of the Interior and the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And now can we go back, please -- or forward to the document that I asked to be put up on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is an Official Note --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think we need to go -- well, we can see it in B/C/S, but it's the second page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- compiled by two gentlemen called Tanasic and Ponorac. Were they members of your SJB?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were members of the traffic police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is one of the documents you provided, wasn't it, to Mr. Sebire during your interview?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, all right. Is this a document that -- that -- that you had in your possession?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here at the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, no, Mr. Tutus.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's when I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, you didn't. Well, I --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I mean, I can take you to the part of the interview where you provided Mr. Sebire with this. Do you want me to do that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No need. When I was interviewed in Banja Luka as a suspect, a suspected member of a joint criminal enterprise, I used in that interview some material that I had in my possession. And then a representative of the OTP, a gentleman and a lady were there, asked me to hand them over. If that's what I said during the interview, then I agree. But I'm not sure. I don't remember giving this to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Because this is a report from, you say, two people who you think were members of the traffic division who had stopped a vehicle in which a driver was carrying a licence in the name of Imamovic. He told these officers that he was a member of the special forces, Ministry of the Interior special forces, on the way back from the front. And according to these officers, when they were checking the cards -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we go back to the first page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This man said: "Call Stojan Zupljanin or Kesic for me so that I can talk to them. Who are you to stop me?" Can you just remind the Court of whom Kesic was?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which Kesic he was referring to. But there was Nedeljko Kesic, chief of the national security service.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And the 65 ter of this one, Your Honours, is 2506.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P10182 [sic], Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next document, please, 2507.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is another Official Note compiled by some people called Gotovac and Skrbo. Again, do you know who they were?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know who Gotovac was, but I can't remember who Skrbo was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, again, this is another document you provided to the OTP. It's a complaint of the 20th of June about someone wearing the Special Police unit uniform, claiming to be a member. Two other people who were in the same uniform stealing gasoline. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the note.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: When you got these Official Notes from members of your station, would these be turned into reports and sent to the CSB or anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such police information was forwarded to the crime police that Zoran Josic was in charge of. Several pieces of such information are used to form a collective report. The notes were sent to the CSB and after a certain period of time, you'd have a special note that would be compiled. The chief of the centre would ask for such reports, and, in accordance with the law, we took appropriate measures that were prescribed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is the 20th of June, and I don't think there's any note about it, for reasons that will become apparent. But on the 16th of June, was there an incident which took place at the Mejdan police station involving members of either the SOS or the Special Police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got a document on the screen, but there was an incident at the Mejdan station.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I don't think you gave us a document about this, but can I just ask you briefly to tell the Court what happened at Mejdan police station.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some members of the SOS group arrived there. They entered the station, the police station. There was some sort of discussion between them and the duty officer in the station. Then the station commander got involved, Petar Tanazevic was his name, and an attempt was made to calm down the situation. One of the men involved was a drug addict in Banja Luka. He said he would throw a grenade in the police station. He had some sort of explosive device. Weapons were then used and someone killed. If that's what have you in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. Were the -- the people killed, did they include somebody called Nenad Kakjut, K-a-k-j-u-t [sic]?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the surname is Kajkut, but I can't remember the names of those killed. I can remember one of the person, Vedran Mandic, but as for the other names, no, I can't remember them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I move, please, next in this series of documents to -- did I ask for the last one to be -- the one of the 20th of June. Can I have that admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 2507 becomes Exhibit P1083. And may I just correct for the record the previous one, 65 ter 2506 become Exhibit P1082 and not P10182, as it was said before by mistake. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we now have 2508 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's actually dated -- it's another Official Note which has at the top -- so this is presumed to be it was delivered one to the crime department, one to the CSB chief, and I can't read the third person to whom this was meant to go. Official Note, again 20th of June, about the Special Police detachment.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. And it's -- this is an incident that took place at the Centar police station, not unlike what you just described that happened at Mejdan. Some officers were checking a vehicle. They found someone from the intervention group.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And then if we go, please, in the next page in English. It's the same page at the bottom in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He'd been taken to the police station, Mr. Racic, and then at quarter to midnight, he came back with two other men, asked why members of the special unit were taken to the centre, takes out a pistol - this is Mr. Racic - saying that he would kill you -- "would kill us." This is the reporting, and so on and so forth. And it's signed - if we go to the last page in English and the second page in B/C/S - by Mr. Lipovac. Were you made aware of this incident?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I signed the note, initialed it and to whom it should be forwarded, to the CSB, to the crime police and to the archives. You weren't able to read that at the bottom. It says "Here," that means the archives. So that was a note that was sent to the centre because their people were involved, and according to the rules on responsibility, they had to receive this. And it was sent to the crime service so that they could take the necessary legal measures. And then there was a special report that was compiled on the basis of several notes of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now this was -- as with the Mejdan incident, although people had died there, this was a major incident, was it, in -- as far as the Special Police were concerned, threatening other police officers?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I object to this leading question. First, when the witness answered the question about the previous incident and about who was killed, he didn't mention Special Police units. He mentioned SOS members. Those are different things, and my learned friend is trying to confuse these two separate things. So if a question is being put and if my colleague wants to place it into context, she should correctly refer to the transcript. The witness mentioned to SOS members and not to Special Police members.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm not -- sorry. I was conflating not the two groups but the nature of the incident and that, I hope, was fairly clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But, Ms. Korner, Mr. Krgovic's question is relevant and I would like to put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Because all the incidents that you have described in the last four documents that you have been pulling up on the screen relate to irregular activities carried out by members of the Special Police, and so that begs the question whether the perpetrators of these irregularities were former SOS members; namely, from the group that, we heard earlier this morning, had been transferred into a Special Police unit. Can you confirm whether the members of the SOS continued to misbehave even after their inclusion into the Special Police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The event I described at the Mejdan police station in which men were killed, well, the people killed were SOS members, and the investigative judge completed this affair. But as for the other incidents before me, the note shows that these incidents concern individual members of the Special Police. It says allegedly members. So certain things have to be checked, naturally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So do I understand you correctly that you are unable to say whether these irregularities were committed by SOS members? You simply don't know. Is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer is as I stated in the note. If someone says that a member of a special detachment is involved, it means that the centre is responsible for this and we have to forward the relevant material to that centre. That when reports are sent to the crime police, then the crime police has to check the situation in the field and to take legal measures. On the basis of the note, I can't claim that it was a SOS member or member of the Special Police or someone who had assumed a false identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Back to you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Your Honours, I want to move on fairly quickly, so may I simply ask that this is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P1084, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Very quickly, please, document 20 -- sorry, 2509.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As a result of the last-described incident, if we look at the last page, please, this document was sent to you, the CSB chief, and various -- the public security chief, by the shift and guard duty leaders and traffic safety police. And it was about how to increase security, as a result of this Racic incident. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we go back to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that right, Mr. Tutus?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean whether the contents are correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Whether -- this was a report that was prepared, was it at your request or anybody else's, on how security had to be increased in the building which housed both the CSB and SJB to prevent a further incident?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security of the CSB and SJB building was the responsibility of the CSB. There was a platoon for the security of the individuals and facilities and they were responsible to provide such security. The note is the result of the work of several authorised policemen, and they have indicated certain problems and forwarded this to the chief of the police station and of the centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Okay. And it's another one of the documents that you handed over, isn't it, to the OTP?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. It doesn't make any difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
