utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P1085, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look at another document that you gave to Sebire.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 2510, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is the 21st of June, so the day after the incident at the police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's Official Note, Your Honour, sorry. Can you see it at the top?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Police -- signed by police officers Copic and Stojinic. Did you know them, Mr. Tutus?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. But I'm familiar with this note. It's one of a series of notes that policemen in the field compiled.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And, again, it's somebody from the -- somebody who says that he's member of the Special Police and who wanted his wife arrested.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we have that, please, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P1086, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 2511, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, are you having a whole batch of Official Notes that you wish to have entered into exhibits or admitted into evidence that all relate to the same pattern of misconduct by alleged members of the Special Police unit?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Isn't there a faster way or a smarter way in which we can do this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, this is the last one, in fact, so -- but I'm quite happy just to put it in because I want to come -- there's a full report about -- that relates to all of this, which I'm coming to next. Your Honours, if I can just ask that the next document, which is yet another report of an incident like this, be admitted and marked. Yes. The 65 ter number is 2511. Can that just be made an exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, so admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And can we now come, please, to -- 2512, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So 65 ter 2510 becomes Exhibit P1086; and 65 ter 2511 becomes Exhibit P1087, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we have now 2512.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we look at the second page, in English and B/C/S, your report, is that right, Mr. Tutus, to Mr. Zupljanin?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we go back to the front page.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, in fact, you list all the incidents where we've just looked at them, the Official Notes, and also some others, it looks like. And you say at the beginning of the first paragraph: "We have already informed you" -- well, let's go back a bit. "Recently, in May and June 1992, the Banja Luka SJB registered cases of negative behaviour by Banja Luka CSB Special Police detachment members, which in certain cases contain elements of offences or crimes. We have already informed you of this on several occasions in dispatches and memos." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And it looks like nothing had happened, so you wrote this on the 24th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, obviously it is misleading.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: This is not -- this happens because -- this doesn't -- what seems from the other documents that nothing was happened. That was my objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before you wrote this to Mr. Zupljanin, on the 24th of June, had Mr. Zupljanin done anything in respect of any of the complaints that you say you had made to him earlier?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't responsible for verifying how my superior performed his duties, what he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But you -- sorry. You say in that first paragraph: "We've already informed you on several occasion in dispatches and memos." What prompted you to write this letter, or put in this report, rather?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the last page of this note, the last paragraph, you can see that there you have the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Let's look, please, at the second page again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You say, as you say, in the last paragraph: "In accordance with your dispatches," 29th of May, 8th of June, "we sincerely hope will you undertake measures which fall under your jurisdiction and that such unwelcome situations will disappear ..." Now, for you to write that, had anything -- had any measures been taken?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first sentence I said, We are fully confident that you want the service to function in accordance with the rules on the work of organs of the interior and the rules on the conduct of your employees, and so on and so forth. What I wanted to say is, well, the note shows that the centre made a request. I referred to their dispatches. They asked us to forward this to them. It's the result of the previous information and we're providing them with a more overall report, and we expect them to take certain measures for which they are responsible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What would you have expected to have happened to the people who arrived -- who arrived in the Centar police station and threatened one of the officers with a gun?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this should be checked. There should be an internal investigation. They should -- there should be criminal reports filed, and they should be removed, naturally, from the service.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Had any of that happened?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. With your leave, I know that the SJB, on a number of occasions, filed criminal reports against former members of that detachment. We did this frequently and together with employees from the CSB, from the crime police of the CSB. There were such reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want to know if those reports were taken anywhere, whether any of these people, to your knowledge, either removed from the Special Police or actually prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were cases of criminal prosecution. The SJB filed relevant reports. As whether for there were disciplinary measures, as for whether people were removed from special detachments, I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, given that you were forwarding all these complaints to Stojan Zupljanin, didn't you make any further inquiries to find out whether anything was happening about whether these people, who, on the face of it, were committing serious criminal offences?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally didn't try to find this out. I had other responsibilities. There were a lot of things happening. The situation was difficult. But at a meeting of the expanded professional council, we had to discuss the behaviour of certain individuals, so the chief of the centre asked us to provide him with all the information that we had about such cases and then he would deal with it. I don't know what he did, but I assume that they continued to look into the matters. I personally wasn't interested in the case, in the subject.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, we'll look a little later at the report that you wrote in 1993 about all this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But can I ask, Your Honours, that that be marked and admitted. And can we move, please, to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked. I don't know if -- you said you're returning to an aspect of this, Ms. Korner, but could I ask the witness whether my understanding of his answers to your last series of questions is that, notwithstanding that the report to Mr. Zupljanin went out over his signature, that you did not, yourself, satisfy yourself, as to the -- whether there was substance to the complaint and whether you just acted as a conduit in passing on the reports that had been passed up to you, on to Mr. Zupljanin. Is that the -- what I should make of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just -- this would be Exhibit P1 -- 65 ter 2512 becomes Exhibit P1088, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we, then, move through, as quickly as we can, before we come to the next incident with the Special Police, through some of the documents in June, please. Document 2375.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, a document that you provided to the investigator. Now, this is a dispatch addressed to SJBs in the region. It -- it is signed, if we look at the third page in English, it's at the bottom of that page in B/C/S, signed by Stojan -- I say "signed." It has got his signature. And if we go back, please, to the front page in English, on 25th of June, Mr. Zupljanin is purporting to alter the jurisdictional activities of the SJBs. Is that right? Because if you look at the third paragraph in English: "The criminal acts which used to fall under the jurisdiction of the higher courts, murder, robbery, violent robbery, looting," et cetera, "I hereby transfer to the jurisdiction of the public security stations." Now can you explain to the Court the relevance and the importance of this purported order.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what matters is that there was a change in the Law on Regular Courts. And since our rule on internal organisation regulates the relationship between the CSBs and public security stations, then this causes a change in jurisdiction. And public security stations are now instructed to take on cases that fell previously under the jurisdiction of higher courts and that used to be dealt with by CSBs, Security Services Centres.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, in your view, was that a change that could be made by Mr. Zupljanin as chief of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it could not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I replied in writing to this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Saying what?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I invoked the relevant legislation. And I said that with the numbers we have, we cannot take on such tasks. I asked for an expansion of the staffing regulations and a proper procedure to be envisaged in the rules; but, of course, it did not relieve us of the responsibility to deal with all crimes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you take the matter any further? In other words, did you go above the CSB for any kind of instructions?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have before me the letter I wrote, but I believe I also informed the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And do you remember -- do you mean the letter was addressed to both the minister of the interior and the -- and the CSB?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I don't know that you provided us with the letter, Mr. Tutus, that you wrote, but ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please. It is an exhibit, is it? Oh, I'm sorry. I'm told it's 10 -- could I have P1015 up on the screen after this has been admitted and marked. Oh, that is an exhibit. Oh, I see. I'm sorry, I'm told it is already an exhibit. I thought that the letter from ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, if you'd -- you may have provided with us a letter, but if so, I'm afraid I don't seem to have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Korner, if we could just have the exhibit number of this -- the last document?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I thought about four people had said it was 1015.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Yes, let's go back, again, to the -- the Special Police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we have up, please, document 2690.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is a -- addressed to the chief of the Security Service Centre, dated the 1st of July. And is that signed by Mr. Josic, your chief of crime police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is sent to the chief of the Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. By?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "To the CSB, chief."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I'm just asking about Mr. Josic. He was your head of the crime section, chief of the crime section in the SJB. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, again, I'm not going to trouble the Court to go through this. It's -- it's a long list of people and offences they have committed, and it's much in the line of the last ones that we saw. Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P1089, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, and I'm sorry, we did have your letter. I thought I had seen it somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we have up 2376.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You did give it to us.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Dated the 2nd of July. So you sent it a few days after this order by Mr. Zupljanin. Addressed, as you say, rightly to the chief of the CSB and the Serbian Republic MUP, the Ministry of Interior. And, in fact, you say you can't accept this, unless there's an increase in your staffing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, sorry, we need to go over to the third page in B/C/S. The last page. There we are. Your Honours, could that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P1090, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If you're about to move on, Ms. Korner, it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, if I may, inasmuch as this witness's testimony is not going to be completed today, there are two matters with which we must deal which I would just as easily deal with now rather than at the end of today's sitting.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The first is this. Recently the Prosecution has brought to the attention of the Senior Legal Officer of the Chamber the fact that a document of the Prosecution Rule 65 ter exhibit list has not yet been disclosed to the Defence, and let me interrupt myself, I think we should be in private session. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The second, counsel would be aware and it is something that I would have had to have notified the witness of before -- at today's -- when we would have adjourned for today, that for administrative reasons we are unable to resume this trial tomorrow. Upon today's adjournment we would continue on Thursday. And the Chamber would invite -- I should probably say urge, request, whatever the appropriate word is to underline the urgency of what I'm about to say - counsel for the Prosecution and for the Defence to use tomorrow to begin preparing for the information of the Chamber their estimates -- their respective estimates as to the progress and conclusion of this trial. Trial note -- that is both the Prosecution and the Defence. And we would wish to have in writing from the parties by close of business on Thursday. Following that, the Chamber is seeking to arrange a 65 ter meeting on Friday morning. You would recall that we resume the trial on Friday afternoon, in order to deal with the -- in order to -- to discuss and finally resolve and communicate onward to the -- to those responsible for the consequential administrative arrangements the future conduct of this trial. So your written submissions by close of business on Thursday; and we would seek to meet mid morning, or 11.00 on Friday morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just mention that it is going to be very difficult for us to provide an accurate or even remotely accurate estimate because we don't have the estimates of cross-examination for all the remainder of the witnesses. Now that means that -- that the Defence have got to consider how long that will take. So it's not -- realistically, it's not going to be possible to give you a proper estimate. Our best guess is that -- I can say this straight away, that we would finish -- we would hope to finish our case by the end of July or maybe just trickle into the first week or so of the resumed hearings. But without -- without estimates of cross-examination and we just asked for them for the witnesses up until -- that we have listed, we can't really say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We're not unappreciative of the challenges that this poses to both sides. But counsel would appreciate that the Chamber itself, as part of the -- as part of the whole business of what the Tribunal is about, is required to communicate information onward. And working from the front to the back, as it were, we would need your input in terms of being able ourselves to indicate to the Registry where we expect we are going, and that why we are inviting you to use tomorrow to -- in addition to whatever else you had arranged to do, to get an estimate - and we appreciate it is only an estimate - to us by Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It is perhaps helpful, Ms. Korner, to tell you that until now, end of February more or less, the Defence took, more or less, the 100 per cent of the chief time. Little bit more, but not much. 10 per cent more. So that can be of -- can be useful in your estimates for the future.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I mean, as I say, Your Honours, I mean, we can give you a rough estimate but no more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So you may continue, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm now going ask you, Mr. Tutus, to look at the lengthy report that you prepared in 1993 about the Special Police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And that is exhibit -- it's already been made an exhibit, 628.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, just one correction. Former members, in relation to this document. It's about former members, not members.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In 1993, I agree, they weren't members because it had been disbanded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't -- I don't understand this. Perhaps I -- but is it former members, or is it former S -- former CSB? In the -- in the title of the document it is former CSB, so I can -- it -- it could be members at the very moment --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I don't want the Crisis Staff of Sanski Most, please. I want Exhibit P628, which should be 65 ter 284.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: 284, yes. Information on registered illegal activities of the members.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What has come up on my screen is Sanski Most Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'm just taking the title of your document. I'm not on the -- on the -- on the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I see, you're reading it. Yes. Your Honour is absolutely right. It does say: "Former Banja Luka Security Services Centre" on the document. You can now see it on the screen. So maybe I was too hasty to agree with Mr. Krgovic. But I agree with Mr. Krgovic that in 1993, when this report was written, in May, theoretically, in any event, the Banja Luka Special Police force had been abandoned -- had been - I have forgotten what the word is now - abolished.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. But it's -- this is -- Mr. Tutus, I know you're familiar with this report. This is addressed to Ministry of the Interior. It's dated the 5th of May, 1993. Can I ask how you came to put this report into the ministry?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the public security sector, Tomislav Kovac, called me and asked me to prepare a comprehensive report on the conduct of the members of the former detachment of Special Police, because they were also bound by this instruction on mutual information, and he thought he should have a comprehensive report. So I gave this assignment to the CID. They prepared this comprehensive report, and I instructed them to provide one copy to the public security sector, to Tomo Kovac who asked for it, and one copy to the chief of the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now, in this information, you list all the -- the -- the matters that we have looked at already in the reports, plus some other matters, and it's about two of those other matters that I wish to ask you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we turn to -- in English, to page 13; and in the B/C/S version, to page 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, the -- at the top of the page, it's quite difficult in English to work out how to do this. But it talks about the arrest of two people called -- at the top of the English page, not in your page. It's above paragraph 23. Dragojevic, Miroslav and Jokic, Ljubomir having been arrested and the Banja Luka public security station filing criminal charges. And it goes on to say: "Members of the special purpose police detachment of the Banja Luka Security Services Centre carried out an attack on the prison and have snatched the members of the same detachment from prison. In such a way, they have prevented the investigating judge from taking legal action." And then on paragraph 23, on the 21st of July, 1992, around 1400 hours, in the Tunjice settlement in Banja Luka, a group of some 30 members of the special purpose police detachment of the CSB Banja Luka have committed the crime of enabling the escape of an imprisoned person. They drove in the armoured carrier and six cars and stopped in front of the Banja Luka county prison -- I think that should probably read municipal, but at the above-mentioned time by threatening with fire-arms. They disarmed five guards and released the two men who had been arrested on the 19th. Now, I'd like a little more detail from you, Mr. Tutus, about this incident, as you gave to the investigator in interview. How did you find out about the arrest of these men?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at home when I was informed by the chief of the CID of the public security station Banja Luka, Zoran Josic, that the said persons were brought in to the police station and that Zdravko Samardzija, one of the commanding officers of the special detachment, was accompanying them, and he asked these persons -- for these persons to be detained because they were responsible for a number of serious crimes in the area in Banja Luka. I asked Chief Josic if there was enough evidence for that and he said --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry to interrupt you. But you said "he said." Was that Samardzija or Mr. -- your -- your CID man? I've forgotten, I'm sorry. Josic. Thank you. Was that Mr. Josic or Samardzija who asked for them to be detained?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Samardzija asked from Josic that these men be detained, and Josic consulted me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I see. And what then happened?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked Zoran Josic if there was enough evidence against them, if their detention would be lawful and if the CSB agreed with that. He answered that the CSB was in agreement, and since these crimes had been committed by them in the area of the public security station of Banja Luka, there were sufficient grounds for them to be remanded in custody. I agreed that this should be done. Josic signed the appropriate decision, and these persons were remanded in custody.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What was the next thing that happened?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day, two senior men from that detachment came to my home, asking me that these men be released, and they said their colleagues were making this demand. I refused. He said that Chief Zupljanin was in agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Pause there. Who were the two senior men who came --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last sentence, the very last one.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could you repeat your last sentence.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two members of that command of the Special Police detachment came to my home, namely, Lukic, whose first name I don't remember, and I think the other one was Dubocanin. At least I think it was Dubocanin. Lukic was certainly the other one, the commander of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was that the Dubocanin who you mentioned as a member of the SOS, in April, or was that his brother, Slobodan?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slobodan, the one who wore a hat. But I'm not sure about that second piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Anyhow, they said that Chief Zupljanin agreed. What did you do?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told them that I couldn't accept that and that I would not sign a decision on their release. That the competent court should decide on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So what happened then?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, sometime late that night, I got a call from Chief Zupljanin, making inquiries about the case, and he told me we should look into it and see if it were possible to release them from the prison, because there is unrest in that unit and there was a danger that they might leave the separation line. I don't know exactly where they were deployed. I said these men had been detained at their request in the first place, and I would not agree to this manner of their release. But since he was my superior officer, I told him that if he thinks still that it is justified, he should give me a proper instruction in writing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And did you get that instruction?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That night, a dispatch arrived from the operations duty service, but I did not find in that dispatch any elements of an order. I found it to be a request for me to reconsider, because this unit could abandon the line of separation. However, I did not find any elements justifying their release, so I did not do it. And I also informed, in parallel, the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: About the arrest. Or about the order from -- the request, as you put it, from Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I consulted the minister. That was my legal obligation. I consulted him about Zupljanin's request to consider the possibility of releasing those men because the unit was threatening or -- or could possibly abandon the separation line.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And did you speak to the minister himself?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, communications were very bad. There were breakdowns and there was one at the time. I couldn't directly contact the minister so I went to the communications centre. I asked the operator to connect me with the minister through other means of communication that Republika Srpska had at its disposal at the time, and he did put me through to General Tolimir, through some sort of military communications, and from General Tolimir, I asked the connection to Minister Stanisic. I told him what it was all about, that I wanted his opinion, and he said he would call me back. And ten minutes later, or less, I got feedback from General Tolimir that Minister Stanisic agrees with my decision that they should stay in prison and that the court should decide upon any further course of action.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We'll look at the document that you received from Zupljanin in a moment but I want to stick with this document. So you declined to release them. What then happened?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day, sometime around noon, one group of those men came outside the district prison, and by using force they disarmed the guards and released those two who were detained.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: As described in your report. Now, as I say, we'll look at a few more documents about this incident in a moment. But one of the incidents you also mentioned in your report is a kidnapping and killing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we go to page 16 in the English. And, sorry, can we go, please, to page 9. Sorry, yes, page 9.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, I think there's an error in the translation, because the paragraph that talks about the kidnapping of Milan Kocic. Anyhow. Says in English, on the 1st of April, 1992, but I think we'll see that it's 1993. Is that right? If we look at the original. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot determine the date now, but I remember the incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, it -- because it looks like that -- that the -- the arrest and the reference number for the proceedings was the 9th of the 4th, 1993. That's quite clear in the -- in the B/C/S -- in the Cyrillic. But the people who had been arrested for that, Mr. Damjanovic, Mr. Bosancic and Zeljko Kajkut, they were all people against whom you had issued complaints about before, weren't they, or at least some of them, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if that's written in the reports that we had discussed before, I believe it must be so, but I can't remember who did what individually.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But it looks as though - and tell us, please, Mr. Tutus - whether or not the unit had been disbanded, the members of that unit were still going on committing criminal offences throughout 1992 and into 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe this is a leading question. It's about members of a unit, in the question of the Prosecutor, where as the document does not mention any members of any unit. Second, this is 1993. Why would it be relevant? As far as can I see, this is about people of the same ethnicity. Why are we now talking about events from 1993 when it's outside of the period of the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, because the point that we're seeking to make is that despite the series of complaints and criminal reports that were put in, these men were still at liberty. That's the point I'm making.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But where is the evidence of that? If the Prosecution says that criminal complaints had been filed against these people previously, let them show a document. We don't have any evidence that any of these people had been the subject of an investigation before.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we look, please, at -- I think we'd have to go back to ... I'm sorry, Your Honour. Rather than waste time, can I look for the document at the end of the day, and I'll come back to this tomorrow. Thank you very much. Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This report ends, if we look, please, at the last page in English. And the last page in B/C/S as well, sorry. I'm sorry, before we do that, the whole thing had started off by a complaint about what was happening in Karanovac. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one of the passages in this report is certainly that inhabitants of Karanovac were complaining against the conduct of individual members of the former detachment of the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. I'm' sorry, then we should look at that as well, please, and then I'll go back.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we look at page 18 in English and the penultimate page in B/C/S. It's page 10, I think. Got it. Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You say that: "Considering the fact that before the creation of this information we did not receive the list of former members of the special purposes police detachment from the Security Services Centre Banja Luka, authorised employees ... obtained data that the ... following 15 persons from the territory of the local community Karanovac were members of this detachment." And you list those people there. Is that right? And the 15 --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we go to the next page in English. Nenad is the last -- Kajkut, employed in the CSB Banja Luka. All right. Now can we -- sorry, the last page in each of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where does it say in the document that Kajkut, one of those mentioned, was employed in the centre in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: According to the translation I have -- sorry, we'll have to go back to it, as I can't read Cyrillic. We need -- sorry, we need -- yes, can we go back to the page 15. Could we look at 15. Does that say "employed in the CSB Banja Luka"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But the context in which it is read. This is a list of members who were from the local commune of Karanovac, not a list of persons involved in criminal activities. This is a list of persons from Karanovac who were involved in the CSB, not involved in criminal activities. That's the point of my objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's not what you said. That's slightly different.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's written in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's slightly different. Sorry, your objection was it didn't say he was employed in the CSB. Do you now withdraw that objection?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: That is what the transcript records your objection as being or having been, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You know what the point is, Your Honours. The Prosecutor, when she was reading this document, was reading the next page, saying -- in fact talking about the involvement of certain members of the CSB in criminal activities. And then she referred him to the previous page, another part of the document listing persons from the local commune of Karanovac who were involved in criminal activities thus creating a confusion, implying that Nenad Kajkut was involved in criminal activities. That is the essence of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I didn't get that impression. But if it is possible that someone following the line of question may have been so confused, then perhaps Ms. Korner it may have been necessary to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. To follow -- I have been trying to skip because it is a very lengthy document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And, of course, Mr. Krgovic has the advantage over both of us in that the original document he is able to -- to comprehend in its -- in B/C/S. But it seems as if we have passed -- the point has been made and we have moved on, haven't we?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I just wanted -- because I have still got to go and double-check something. But, Your Honour, can I leave this document, except for the last part, and then come back to it, I'm afraid, tomorrow when I have, as it were, correlated everything. Because it is slightly complicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: We're meeting --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, Thursday, Your Honour. Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll tell you what, Mr. Tutus, you have to come back on Thursday. We'll leave this document. I'll come back to that on Thursday morning, if I may, briefly. And can we now look, please, at the document that you received from Mr. Zupljanin, which is 1971.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, I think this is a document that you had with you when you were interviewed. It's dated the 20th of July, and it says: "The security information collected so far indicate that the security situation on the territory of Banja Luka could be disturbed." Now you told us that when you spoke to him, or when he rang you, he was talking about the -- the unit -- I think you said on the front. I need to go back to what you actually said. Yes, leaving the front line. Here the document says that: "The security situation on the territory of Banja Luka could be disturbed."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. He told me over the phone that part of that unit might leave the front line and that could pose a threat to the demarcation line, to the front line.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But the front line wasn't in Banja Luka, was it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say it was in Banja Luka. I said I didn't know in which area they were actually located.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Due to the arrest of these two men: "It is necessary that you release these individuals from detention and inform them to report to the Banja Luka SJB for future operative steps, in other words, escort them to the Banja Luka basic court ... if the above persons fail to report to you at the specified time ..." So you took the words "it is necessary that you release these individuals" not as an order but as a request?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you didn't and we then saw what happened. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P1091, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next document is yet another report dated the 21st of July, about behaviour of the Special Police, signed by Mr. Josic. Rather than going through it, may I just ask that it be admitted as part of that group. It's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The number of this document is -- oh, I'm sorry, it is already admitted. Forget that. Can we look, please, now at document P585, very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's, again -- this is the actual -- another report, sorry, which has sent not only to the CSB but to the Serbian Republic of BiH MUP, a report signed by Mr. Josic, which talks about another criminal report of robberies and the like and it's signed by Mr. Josic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And, again, can we just -- Your Honours, in fact can we just note that and -- it is already admitted. Sorry, I slightly confused myself. Could we look, please, at the exhibit which has already been done, P586, which is the Glas report of this whole unfortunate incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I want to ask you about one part of it, we need to go to the second page in English. All of this is contained on one page in the newspaper. Mr. Ecim was apparently interviewed. And it says: "The entire command appealed to ... Radic, Vukic, Radoslav Brdjanin to insist on the arrested men being released. But [sic] Mr. Tutus refused all these requests." Were you contacted as well by Mr. Radic, Mr. Vukic and Mr. Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: President Radic did contact me. Dr. Vukic was with him. He was in his company, but he said nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And were they asking for the release of these men as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: President Radic only asked me for information about what had happened, and I told him what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And after you told him what had happened, did he ask you, or didn't he, to release these men?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So this is inaccurate reporting by the -- the -- well, I suppose it -- not quite. Just says "Mr. Tutus refused all requests." Did somebody called Kojic come to the police station?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what about Ecim? Did he come to the police station as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't in my office. We didn't see -- I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, were you told he had gone somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was never mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And then the report goes on to say: "Tutus told me," that must be Kojic, I suppose, "that no one could order him around and he tore up the decision annulling custody at the same time, says Ecim." So Ecim appears to be saying to the newspaper he was there. "At the same time he placed the whole police force on full alert, with guns at the ready, and threw Kojic out of his office." Is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the discussion between myself and the chief of the centre, when he promised he would draft this order to have them released, I went to the office and Chief Josic was there. And then Kojic appeared. I didn't know him at the time. He said he was from the detachment. He said, I've come pursuant to a decision according to which our comrades should be released from prison. I said that I didn't have such a decision from the chief of the centre. I said I had received the dispatch from the operative duty service, and the dispatch didn't show that there was a direct order for their release. I said that I wouldn't do that and that there was no decision on their release from detention. Perhaps a decision had been prepared on the desk but I really threw it into the basket. He left, and Ecim simply did not appear at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Yes, thank you. That's all I want to ask about that document, which I think is already an exhibit. And the next one is an exhibit so I don't have to ask you about that. While I'm looking for the next document, can I just ask you this, Mr. Tutus. During the meetings that you had with Mr. Zupljanin and the other chiefs of the SJBs, did you meet Simo Drljaca from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were at the professional council of the centre together. That's where we would meet.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, at some stage during August of 1992, was there discussion about the information that was being requested from the CSB and then the SJBs as to any detention or collection centres that were in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the details. Perhaps there were such discussions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, do you remember any conversation - again, can I remind you, you were asked about this in interview - between Simo Drljaca and Stojan Zupljanin about the collection centres or detention facilities that had been set up in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember a discussion between the chief of the centre, Zupljanin, and Simo Drljaca. It was in a gymnasium. It was quite a large gathering, and before the meeting started, Chief Zupljanin issued a warning to Simo Drljaca. He said, What did you do down there, Simo? You will be held to account for that. Something to that effect. What the subject was was not quite clear. I couldn't draw any conclusions. I don't know whether it was about collection centres or something else. But, in any event, he issued this warning to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And what was the reaction of Mr. Drljaca to that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He reacted in a fairly and aggressive way. But three days later, Zupljanin repeated this to him at a different meeting of the professional council. He repeated the same thing. He was obviously dissatisfied with something that was going on there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did -- did Mr. Zupljanin ever explain to you that he visited any of these collection centres?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, but the witness's answer hasn't been recorded in the transcript, Simo Drljaca's reaction. He said he was aggressive. This entire part of the transcript is missing so could the witness perhaps repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, could you tell us again what Simo Drljaca's reaction was when you say that Mr. Zupljanin told him he would be held -- he'd be held -- you will be held to account for that.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that Simo reacted in a nervous and aggressive manner. In an inappropriate manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And in what way? I mean, what did he say or do?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was unpleasant, brazen. I can't repeat what his exact words were. That was over 15 years ago, but I do know that he swore. He said something that was -- that was brazen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Did your police from your police stations become involved with convoys that were coming from the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which convoys you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: People who had been in places like Trnopolje and were being taken out towards Travnik.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no such information. Perhaps the traffic police station was still part of the SJB or perhaps it was part of the centre. If there were any such convoys, if that police -- that traffic police station was still functional, then it could have organised some sort of transport or escorted some sort of transport, some sort of convoy. So perhaps there were such activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, you looked at the documents. I wasn't going to trouble to show them to you. But -- wouldn't the traffic police have had to sought your authority for this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one sought my authority. But if one was working outside workings hours and if the operative duty service asked for a traffic police patrol in the field to do certain things, to escort a bus, or two, or three, through the territory covered by that traffic station, then, those orders would be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. It's all right. I'm sorry, I need to find that document. Could you have a look very briefly, though, please, at document 232. Now, this is ... This is a document which shows the payroll for August 1992 of the members of the Banja Luka security -- Special Police detachment, containing apparently their signatures. And we see at the top, Lukic and Ecim and Samardzija.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise any names - it may be the same point; I'm going have to double-check - who were drawing pay in August 1992 against whom you had submitted criminal reports way back in June, or Official Notes?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I'm sorry, it's the same problem. I'm going to have to do the double-check. I thought the witness could do this himself but I will have to go back and do the check on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: However, do you -- do you recognise the first three names as members of the CSB Special Police detachment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirko Lukic, Ecim and Samardzija, yes, I know them personally. Lukic was the commander, as far as I know, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just ask that this is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit P1092, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, really I have got very little left to ask except concerning -- trying to trace these two documents but I can't do it, as it were, on my feet, so I wonder if we could adjourn now to resume with what little time I have left on Thursday morning. So I can do this exercise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, in terms of little time I was going to remind you when we took the adjournment at 1.45 that you would have, in fact, exhausted your six hours, so --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: By quarter to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, Your Honour, may I ask, very simply, that I get 15 -- an extra 5, 15 minutes on Thursday morning and we adjourn now, because effectively to do this exercise of tracing the names into this is -- is one that is going to take up time while I'm on my feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tutus, as I -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As you may recall, when I would have been speaking to counsel at the beginning of today's session, for certain administrative reasons we are unable to sit tomorrow. So, therefore, we will take the adjournment now and resume on Thursday morning. And for the information of counsel, we would be sitting in Courtroom I on Thursday. So, Mr. Tutus, I remind you of what I said at the adjournment yesterday, about your not discussing the case with anyone outside of the court and not communicating with counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
